claim: UBIAD1 synthesizes the vitamin K subtype menaquinone-4 (MK-4).
source: UbiA prenyltransferase domain-containing protein-1 (UBIAD1) synthesizes the vitamin K subtype menaquinone-4 (MK-4).
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations to previous work (Hirota et al., 2013; Nakagawa et al., 2010) in the introduction.

claim: UBIAD1 inhibits endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-associated degradation (ERAD) of ubiquitinated HMG CoA reductase (HMGCR).
source: Previous studies in cultured cells (Schumacher et al., 2015) revealed that UBIAD1 also inhibits endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-associated degradation (ERAD) of ubiquitinated HMG CoA reductase (HMGCR), the rate-limiting enzyme of the mevalonate pathway that produces cholesterol and essential nonsterol isoprenoids.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Schumacher et al., 2015.

claim: Homozygous germ-line elimination of the Ubiad1 gene caused embryonic lethality in mice.
source: Gene knockout studies were previously attempted to explore the function of UBIAD1 in mice; however, homozygous germ-line elimination of the Ubiad1 gene caused embryonic lethality.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citation to Nakagawa et al., 2014 in the introduction.

claim: Homozygous deletion of Ubiad1 is produced in knockin mice expressing ubiquitination/ERAD-resistant HMGCR.
source: We now report that homozygous deletion of Ubiad1 is produced in knockin mice expressing ubiquitination/ERAD-resistant HMGCR.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data in Table 1 and Figure 2.

claim: Embryonic lethality of Ubiad1 deficiency results from depletion of mevalonate-derived products owing to enhanced ERAD of HMGCR rather than from reduced synthesis of MK-4.
source: Thus, embryonic lethality of Ubiad1 deficiency results from depletion of mevalonate-derived products owing to enhanced ERAD of HMGCR rather than from reduced synthesis of MK-4.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, inferred from the rescue of embryonic lethality by ERAD-resistant HMGCR.

claim: Vitamin K serves as a cofactor for γ-carboxyglutamyl carboxylase.
source: Vitamin K refers to a group of lipophilic molecules that serve as a cofactor for γ-carboxyglutamyl carboxylase, which converts specific glutamate residues in a limited set of proteins to γ-carboxyglutamate (Shearer and Newman, 2014; Shearer and Okano, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Shearer and Newman, 2014 and Shearer and Okano, 2018.

claim: γ-carboxyglutamate post-translational modification is obligatory for biological functions of vitamin K-dependent proteins (VKDPs).
source: This post-translational modification is obligatory for biological functions of resultant vitamin K-dependent proteins (VKDPs), some of which play key roles in blood coagulation.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Some VKDPs play key roles in blood coagulation.
source: This post-translational modification is obligatory for biological functions of resultant vitamin K-dependent proteins (VKDPs), some of which play key roles in blood coagulation.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: VKDPs are implicated in processes ranging from bone and cardiovascular mineralization to energy metabolism and inflammation.
source: Other VKDPs are implicated in processes ranging from bone and cardiovascular mineralization to energy metabolism and inflammation (Booth, 2009; Shearer and Okano, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Booth, 2009 and Shearer and Okano, 2018.

claim: Vitamin K may exert direct effects on gene expression, signal transduction, and cellular regulation.
source: In addition, vitamin K may exert direct effects on gene expression, signal transduction, and cellular regulation.
evidence: This is stated as a speculative possibility in the introduction.

claim: All vitamin K forms include a common 2-methyl-1,4-naphthoquinone ring structure known as menadione (MD).
source: All vitamin K forms include a common 2-methyl-1,4-naphthoquinone ring structure known as menadione (MD) (Figure 1A) and are distinguished from one another by length and saturation of the side chain attached at the 3-carbon position on the ring (Shearer and Newman, 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 1A, supported by citation to Shearer and Newman, 2014.

claim: Vitamin K forms are distinguished from one another by length and saturation of the side chain attached at the 3-carbon position on the ring.
source: All vitamin K forms include a common 2-methyl-1,4-naphthoquinone ring structure known as menadione (MD) (Figure 1A) and are distinguished from one another by length and saturation of the side chain attached at the 3-carbon position on the ring (Shearer and Newman, 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 1A, supported by citation to Shearer and Newman, 2014.

claim: MD is a provitamin form of vitamin K as the side chain is required for vitamin K activity.
source: MD is a provitamin form of vitamin K as the side chain is required for vitamin K activity (Buitenhuis et al., 1990).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Buitenhuis et al., 1990.

claim: Phylloquinone (PK) contains a phytyl side chain.
source: Phylloquinone (PK, also known as vitamin K1) (Figure 1A) contains a phytyl side chain, whereas menaquinones (MKs, collectively referred to as vitamin K2) contain a side chain with 5-carbon isoprenyl units and are named according to the number of these units (e.g., MK-n) (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: Menaquinones (MKs) contain a side chain with 5-carbon isoprenyl units and are named according to the number of these units.
source: Phylloquinone (PK, also known as vitamin K1) (Figure 1A) contains a phytyl side chain, whereas menaquinones (MKs, collectively referred to as vitamin K2) contain a side chain with 5-carbon isoprenyl units and are named according to the number of these units (e.g., MK-n) (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: PK is produced by plants.
source: PK is produced by plants, whereas longer chain MKs (MK-7, MK-9, and MK-11) are predominantly of bacterial origin.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Longer chain MKs (MK-7, MK-9, and MK-11) are predominantly of bacterial origin.
source: PK is produced by plants, whereas longer chain MKs (MK-7, MK-9, and MK-11) are predominantly of bacterial origin.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Invertebrate and vertebrate animals produce MK-4 from dietary PK through a reaction involving side chain removal and re-addition with MD as an intermediate.
source: Invertebrate and vertebrate animals produce MK-4 from dietary PK through a reaction involving side chain removal and re-addition with MD as an intermediate (Al Rajabi et al., 2012; Okano et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Al Rajabi et al., 2012 and Okano et al., 2008.

claim: UBIAD1 is a member of the UbiA superfamily of prenyltransferases.
source: UbiA prenyltransferase domain-containing protein-1 (UBIAD1), a member of the UbiA superfamily of prenyltransferases (Li, 2016), transfers the 20-carbon geranylgeranyl group from geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate (GGpp) to PK-derived MD, thereby producing MK-4 (Hirota et al., 2013; Nakagawa et al., 2010; Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Li, 2016.

claim: UBIAD1 transfers the 20-carbon geranylgeranyl group from geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate (GGpp) to PK-derived MD, thereby producing MK-4.
source: UbiA prenyltransferase domain-containing protein-1 (UBIAD1), a member of the UbiA superfamily of prenyltransferases (Li, 2016), transfers the 20-carbon geranylgeranyl group from geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate (GGpp) to PK-derived MD, thereby producing MK-4 (Hirota et al., 2013; Nakagawa et al., 2010; Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Hirota et al., 2013 and Nakagawa et al., 2010, and illustrated in Figure 1B.

claim: Mutations in human UBIAD1 are associated with Schnyder corneal dystrophy (SCD).
source: The function of UBIAD1 appears to extend beyond its role in MK-4 synthesis, as indicated by association of mutations in human UBIAD1 with Schnyder corneal dystrophy (SCD) (Orr et al., 2007; Weiss et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Orr et al., 2007 and Weiss et al., 2007.

claim: Schnyder corneal dystrophy (SCD) is a rare, autosomal-dominant disease characterized by progressive corneal opacification that results from accumulation of cholesterol.
source: This rare, autosomal-dominant disease is characterized by progressive corneal opacification that results from accumulation of cholesterol.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about SCD.

claim: SCD-associated UBIAD1 inhibits the sterol-accelerated, endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-associated degradation (ERAD) of 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl coenzyme A reductase (HMGCR).
source: In 2015, we showed that SCD-associated UBIAD1 inhibits the sterol-accelerated, endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-associated degradation (ERAD) of 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl coenzyme A reductase (HMGCR) (Schumacher et al., 2015), one of several feedback mechanisms that converge on the enzyme to assure cholesterol homeostasis (Brown and Goldstein, 1980).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Schumacher et al., 2015.

claim: HMGCR is one of several feedback mechanisms that converge on the enzyme to assure cholesterol homeostasis.
source: In 2015, we showed that SCD-associated UBIAD1 inhibits the sterol-accelerated, endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-associated degradation (ERAD) of 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl coenzyme A reductase (HMGCR) (Schumacher et al., 2015), one of several feedback mechanisms that converge on the enzyme to assure cholesterol homeostasis (Brown and Goldstein, 1980).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Brown and Goldstein, 1980.

claim: HMGCR is polytopic and ER-localized.
source: Polytopic, ER-localized HMGCR produces mevalonate, an important intermediate in synthesis of cholesterol and the nonsterol isoprenoids farnesyl pyrophosphate (Fpp) and GGpp that are transferred to many cellular proteins and utilized in synthesis of other nonsterol isoprenoids including MK-4, heme, ubiquinone-10, and dolichol (Goldstein and Brown, 1990; Wang and Casey, 2016) (see Figure 1B).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: HMGCR produces mevalonate, an important intermediate in synthesis of cholesterol and the nonsterol isoprenoids farnesyl pyrophosphate (Fpp) and GGpp.
source: Polytopic, ER-localized HMGCR produces mevalonate, an important intermediate in synthesis of cholesterol and the nonsterol isoprenoids farnesyl pyrophosphate (Fpp) and GGpp that are transferred to many cellular proteins and utilized in synthesis of other nonsterol isoprenoids including MK-4, heme, ubiquinone-10, and dolichol (Goldstein and Brown, 1990; Wang and Casey, 2016) (see Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Goldstein and Brown, 1990 and Wang and Casey, 2016, and illustrated in Figure 1B.

claim: Fpp and GGpp are transferred to many cellular proteins and utilized in synthesis of other nonsterol isoprenoids including MK-4, heme, ubiquinone-10, and dolichol.
source: Polytopic, ER-localized HMGCR produces mevalonate, an important intermediate in synthesis of cholesterol and the nonsterol isoprenoids farnesyl pyrophosphate (Fpp) and GGpp that are transferred to many cellular proteins and utilized in synthesis of other nonsterol isoprenoids including MK-4, heme, ubiquinone-10, and dolichol (Goldstein and Brown, 1990; Wang and Casey, 2016) (see Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Goldstein and Brown, 1990 and Wang and Casey, 2016, and illustrated in Figure 1B.

claim: Sterols accelerate ERAD of HMGCR by stimulating its binding to ER membrane proteins called Insigs.
source: Sterols accelerate ERAD of HMGCR by stimulating its binding to ER membrane proteins called Insigs (Sever et al., 2003a; Sever et al., 2003b).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Sever et al., 2003a and Sever et al., 2003b.

claim: Insig-associated ubiquitin ligases facilitate ubiquitination of HMGCR.
source: Insig-associated ubiquitin ligases facilitate ubiquitination of HMGCR (Jiang et al., 2018; Jo et al., 2011; Song et al., 2005), marking it for extraction across ER membranes and subsequent cytosolic release for ERAD by 26S proteasomes (Morris et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Jiang et al., 2018, Jo et al., 2011, and Song et al., 2005.

claim: Ubiquitination of HMGCR marks it for extraction across ER membranes and subsequent cytosolic release for ERAD by 26S proteasomes.
source: Insig-associated ubiquitin ligases facilitate ubiquitination of HMGCR (Jiang et al., 2018; Jo et al., 2011; Song et al., 2005), marking it for extraction across ER membranes and subsequent cytosolic release for ERAD by 26S proteasomes (Morris et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Morris et al., 2014.

claim: ERAD of HMGCR is enhanced by GGpp, which enhances membrane extraction of the ubiquitinated enzyme.
source: ERAD of HMGCR is enhanced by GGpp, which enhances membrane extraction of the ubiquitinated enzyme (Elsabrouty et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Elsabrouty et al., 2013.

claim: Sterols cause HMGCR to bind UBIAD1.
source: Sterols also cause HMGCR to bind UBIAD1 (Schumacher et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Schumacher et al., 2015.

claim: UBIAD1 binding to HMGCR inhibits the ERAD of HMGCR at a post-ubiquitination step in the reaction.
source: This binding inhibits the ERAD of HMGCR at a post-ubiquitination step in the reaction, thereby permitting continued synthesis of mevalonate for incorporation into nonsterol isoprenoids even when intracellular sterols are abundant (Schumacher et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Schumacher et al., 2018.

claim: UBIAD1 binding to HMGCR permits continued synthesis of mevalonate for incorporation into nonsterol isoprenoids even when intracellular sterols are abundant.
source: This binding inhibits the ERAD of HMGCR at a post-ubiquitination step in the reaction, thereby permitting continued synthesis of mevalonate for incorporation into nonsterol isoprenoids even when intracellular sterols are abundant (Schumacher et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Schumacher et al., 2018.

claim: GGpp triggers release of UBIAD1 from HMGCR.
source: GGpp triggers release of UBIAD1 from HMGCR, which allows for maximal ERAD of HMGCR and translocation of UBIAD1 from the ER to the medial-trans Golgi.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge from previous work.

claim: GGpp-triggered release of UBIAD1 from HMGCR allows for maximal ERAD of HMGCR and translocation of UBIAD1 from the ER to the medial-trans Golgi.
source: GGpp triggers release of UBIAD1 from HMGCR, which allows for maximal ERAD of HMGCR and translocation of UBIAD1 from the ER to the medial-trans Golgi.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge from previous work.

claim: SCD-associated mutations cluster around the membrane-embedded active site of UBIAD1.
source: SCD-associated mutations cluster around the membrane-embedded active site of UBIAD1 (Cheng and Li, 2014; Huang et al., 2014), indicating they may disrupt sensing of GGpp.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Cheng and Li, 2014 and Huang et al., 2014.

claim: SCD-associated mutations in UBIAD1 may disrupt sensing of GGpp.
source: SCD-associated mutations cluster around the membrane-embedded active site of UBIAD1 (Cheng and Li, 2014; Huang et al., 2014), indicating they may disrupt sensing of GGpp.
evidence: This is inferred from the location of mutations and supported by citations.

claim: SCD-associated UBIAD1 is refractory to GGpp-induced release from HMGCR and becomes sequestered in the ER.
source: Indeed, SCD-associated UBIAD1 is refractory to GGpp-induced release from HMGCR and becomes sequestered in the ER (Schumacher et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Schumacher et al., 2016.

claim: Sequestration of SCD-associated UBIAD1 in the ER leads to inhibition of HMGCR ERAD and enhanced synthesis and intracellular accumulation of cholesterol.
source: The resultant inhibition of HMGCR ERAD leads to enhanced synthesis and intracellular accumulation of cholesterol (Schumacher et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Schumacher et al., 2018.

claim: Mouse embryos homozygous for Ubiad1 deficiency failed to survive past embryonic day 7.5.
source: However, mouse embryos homozygous for Ubiad1 deficiency failed to survive past embryonic day 7.5.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from Nakagawa et al., 2014.

claim: ERAD of HMGCR was enhanced in transformed human fibroblasts lacking UBIAD1.
source: We recently observed that the ERAD of HMGCR was enhanced in transformed human fibroblasts lacking UBIAD1 (Schumacher et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Schumacher et al., 2018.

claim: Two independent lines of mice were obtained in which the Ubiad1 gene was disrupted by a 172- (Disrupted Allele A) or 29 bp deletion (Disrupted Allele B) in exon 1.
source: Two independent lines of mice were obtained in which the Ubiad1 gene was disrupted by a 172- (Disrupted Allele A) or 29 bp deletion (Disrupted Allele B) in exon 1 (Figure 2).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, shown in Figure 2.

claim: Disrupted Allele A would produce a protein fragment comprising amino acids 1–39 of UBIAD1 fused to a novel polypeptide of 55 amino acids if transcribed and translated.
source: If transcribed and translated, these alleles would produce protein fragments comprising amino acids 1–38 (Disrupted Allele B) or 1–39 (Disrupted Allele A) of UBIAD1 fused to a novel polypeptide of 55 or 56 amino acids (Figure 2).
evidence: This is predicted based on the genomic deletions shown in Figure 2.

claim: Disrupted Allele B would produce a protein fragment comprising amino acids 1–38 of UBIAD1 fused to a novel polypeptide of 56 amino acids if transcribed and translated.
source: If transcribed and translated, these alleles would produce protein fragments comprising amino acids 1–38 (Disrupted Allele B) or 1–39 (Disrupted Allele A) of UBIAD1 fused to a novel polypeptide of 55 or 56 amino acids (Figure 2).
evidence: This is predicted based on the genomic deletions shown in Figure 2.

claim: Intercrosses of Ubiad1+/- mice produced WT and Ubiad1+/- offspring at a ratio of approximately 1:2, which is consistent with Mendelian segregation.
source: Intercrosses of Ubiad1+/- mice produced WT and Ubiad1+/- offspring at a ratio of approximately 1:2, which is consistent with Mendelian segregation.
evidence: This is supported by the breeding data in Table 1.

claim: Ubiad1-/- offspring were not produced from intercrosses of Ubiad1+/- mice, regardless of disrupted Ubiad1 allele.
source: However, Ubiad1-/- offspring were not produced, regardless of disrupted Ubiad1 allele.
evidence: This is supported by the breeding data in Table 1.

claim: All three expected genotypes (Ubiad1+/+: :HmgcrKi/Ki, Ubiad1+/-: :HmgcrKi/Ki, and Ubiad1-/-: :HmgcrKi/Ki) were produced when Ubiad1+/-: :HmgcrKi/Ki mice were intercrossed.
source: In striking contrast, all three expected genotypes (Ubiad1+/+: :HmgcrKi/Ki, Ubiad1+/-: :HmgcrKi/Ki, and Ubiad1-/-: :HmgcrKi/Ki) were produced when Ubiad1+/-: :HmgcrKi/Ki mice were intercrossed (Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by the breeding data in Table 1.

claim: The observed proportion of +/+ : +/- : -/- Ubiad1 alleles was 137:280:114 (Disrupted Allele A) when Ubiad1+/-: :HmgcrKi/Ki mice were intercrossed.
source: The observed proportion of +/+ : +/- : -/- Ubiad1 alleles was 137:280:114 (Disrupted Allele A) and 23:36:20 (Disrupted Allele B), when the expected proportion is 1:2:1.
evidence: This is supported by the breeding data in Table 1.

claim: The observed proportion of +/+ : +/- : -/- Ubiad1 alleles was 23:36:20 (Disrupted Allele B) when Ubiad1+/-: :HmgcrKi/Ki mice were intercrossed.
source: The observed proportion of +/+ : +/- : -/- Ubiad1 alleles was 137:280:114 (Disrupted Allele A) and 23:36:20 (Disrupted Allele B), when the expected proportion is 1:2:1.
evidence: This is supported by the breeding data in Table 1.

claim: Ubiquitination/ERAD-resistant HMGCR rescues embryonic lethality of Ubiad1 deficiency.
source: These results provide genetic evidence that ubiquitination/ERAD-resistant HMGCR rescues embryonic lethality of Ubiad1 deficiency.
evidence: This is the main conclusion from the breeding experiments shown in Table 1.

claim: Male and female Ubiad1+/- mice exhibited reduced levels of hepatic UBIAD1 protein.
source: Male and female Ubiad1+/- mice exhibited reduced levels of hepatic UBIAD1 protein as expected (Figure 3A, compare lanes 1 and 3 with lanes 2 and 4).
evidence: This is shown in the immunoblot data in Figure 3A.

claim: HMGCR protein was slightly reduced in livers of Ubiad1+/- mice, which likely resulted from enhanced ERAD.
source: HMGCR protein was slightly reduced in livers of the mice (lanes 1–4), which likely resulted from enhanced ERAD.
evidence: This is observed in Figure 3A and interpreted based on known mechanisms.

claim: The level of membrane-bound precursor and nuclear forms of SREBPs remained constant in Ubiad1+/- mice.
source: The level of membrane-bound precursor and nuclear forms of SREBPs remained constant in Ubiad1+/- mice (lanes 5–8 and 9–12).
evidence: This is shown in the immunoblot data in Figure 3A.

claim: Ubiad1+/- mice were indistinguishable from WT littermates and had similar body weights.
source: Despite reduced levels of hepatic UBIAD1 and HMGCR protein, Ubiad1+/- mice were indistinguishable from WT littermates and had similar body weights.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study.

claim: UBIAD1 protein was absent from hepatic membranes of Ubiad1-/-: :HmgcrKi/Ki mice.
source: The absence of UBIAD1 protein from hepatic membranes of Ubiad1-/-: :HmgcrKi/Ki was confirmed in Figure 3B (compare lanes 1–2 and 4–5 with lanes 3 and 6, respectively).
evidence: This is shown in the immunoblot data in Figure 3B.

claim: The amount of HMGCR protein and nuclear SREBPs was varied in livers of Ubiad1-/-: :HmgcrKi/Ki mice.
source: The amount of HMGCR protein and nuclear SREBPs was varied in livers of the animals (lanes 1–18); however, the nature of this variation was not clear.
evidence: This is observed in Figure 3B.

claim: Male Ubiad1-/-: :HmgcrKi/Ki mice were 30% smaller than their Ubiad1+/+: :HmgcrKi/Ki and Ubiad1+/-: :HmgcrKi/Ki littermates at 8 weeks of age.
source: Although ubiquitination/ERAD-resistant HMGCR rescued embryonic lethality of Ubiad1 deficiency, male and female Ubiad1-/-: :HmgcrKi/Ki mice were smaller (30% and 20%, respectively) than their Ubiad1+/+: :HmgcrKi/Ki and Ubiad1+/-: :HmgcrKi/Ki littermates at 8 weeks of age.
evidence: This is shown in the body weight data in Figure 3B.

claim: Female Ubiad1-/-: :HmgcrKi/Ki mice were 20% smaller than their Ubiad1+/+: :HmgcrKi/Ki and Ubiad1+/-: :HmgcrKi/Ki littermates at 8 weeks of age.
source: Although ubiquitination/ERAD-resistant HMGCR rescued embryonic lethality of Ubiad1 deficiency, male and female Ubiad1-/-: :HmgcrKi/Ki mice were smaller (30% and 20%, respectively) than their Ubiad1+/+: :HmgcrKi/Ki and Ubiad1+/-: :HmgcrKi/Ki littermates at 8 weeks of age.
evidence: This is shown in the body weight data in Figure 3B.

claim: Hepatic levels of cholesterol and triglycerides were not globally changed in the absence of Ubiad1.
source: Hepatic levels of cholesterol and triglycerides (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B) as well as most mRNAs encoding SREBPs, SREBP pathway components, and cholesterol/fatty acid synthetic enzymes were not globally changed in the absence of Ubiad1 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Most mRNAs encoding SREBPs, SREBP pathway components, and cholesterol/fatty acid synthetic enzymes were not globally changed in the absence of Ubiad1.
source: Hepatic levels of cholesterol and triglycerides (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B) as well as most mRNAs encoding SREBPs, SREBP pathway components, and cholesterol/fatty acid synthetic enzymes were not globally changed in the absence of Ubiad1 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The mRNA encoding Insig-2a (the major Insig-2 isoform in the liver) was reduced in Ubiad1-deficient mice.
source: Notably, the mRNA encoding Insig-2a (the major Insig-2 isoform in the liver) was reduced, whereas the minor Insig-2b transcript was slightly increased in Ubiad1-deficient mice.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The minor Insig-2b transcript was slightly increased in Ubiad1-deficient mice.
source: Notably, the mRNA encoding Insig-2a (the major Insig-2 isoform in the liver) was reduced, whereas the minor Insig-2b transcript was slightly increased in Ubiad1-deficient mice.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Ubiad1+/+: :HmgcrKi/Ki and Ubiad1+/-: :HmgcrKi/Ki mice gained weight at similar rates up to ~8 weeks post-weaning.
source: The results show that Ubiad1+/+: :HmgcrKi/Ki and Ubiad1+/-: :HmgcrKi/Ki mice gained weight at similar rates up to ~8 weeks post-weaning.
evidence: This is shown in the weight gain data in Figure 3C.

claim: Ubiad1-/-: :HmgcrKi/Ki mice gained weight up to 2 weeks post-weaning (albeit at a reduced rate compared to littermates), after which weight gain plateaued.
source: Ubiad1-/-: :HmgcrKi/Ki mice gained weight up to 2 weeks post-weaning (albeit at a reduced rate compared to littermates), after which weight gain plateaued.
evidence: This is shown in the weight gain data in Figure 3C.

claim: After 7.7 weeks, male and female Ubiad1-/-: :HmgcrKi/Ki mice were 30–40% smaller than Ubiad1+/+: :HmgcrKi/Ki and Ubiad1+/-: :HmgcrKi/Ki littermates.
source: After 7.7 weeks, male and female Ubiad1-/-: :HmgcrKi/Ki mice were 30–40% smaller than Ubiad1+/+: :HmgcrKi/Ki and Ubiad1+/-: :HmgcrKi/Ki littermates.
evidence: This is shown in the weight gain data in Figure 3C.

claim: UBIAD1 was not detected in membranes isolated from the liver, pancreas, brain, kidney, and spleen of Ubiad1-deficient mice.
source: As expected, UBIAD1 was not detected in membranes isolated from the liver, pancreas, brain, kidney, and spleen of Ubiad1-deficient mice (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is shown in the immunoblot data in Figure 4A.

claim: MK-4 accumulated to the highest level in the pancreas of Ubiad1+/+: :HmgcrKi/Ki mice.
source: Figure 4B shows that MK-4, the product of UBIAD1 enzymatic activity, accumulated to the highest level in the pancreas of Ubiad1+/+: :HmgcrKi/Ki mice.
evidence: This is shown in the MK-4 measurement data in Figure 4B.

claim: Lower levels of MK-4 were found in the brain, kidney, spleen, and liver of Ubiad1+/+: :HmgcrKi/Ki mice.
source: Lower levels of MK-4 were found in the brain, kidney, spleen, and liver of the animals.
evidence: This is shown in the MK-4 measurement data in Figure 4B.

claim: MK-4 failed to accumulate to detectable levels in tissues of Ubiad1-deficient mice.
source: In contrast, MK-4 failed to accumulate to detectable levels in tissues of Ubiad1-deficient mice.
evidence: This is shown in the MK-4 measurement data in Figure 4B.

claim: Ubiad1-/-: :HmgcrKi/Ki mice exhibited elevated levels of ALT (1.6-fold) in the serum compared to Ubiad1+/+: :HmgcrKi/Ki littermates.
source: Compared to Ubiad1+/+: :HmgcrKi/Ki littermates, Ubiad1-/-: :HmgcrKi/Ki mice exhibited elevated levels of ALT (1.6-fold) and AST (>5 fold) in the serum (Figure 4C and D; Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is shown in the blood chemistry data in Figure 4C and D.

claim: Ubiad1-/-: :HmgcrKi/Ki mice exhibited elevated levels of AST (>5 fold) in the serum compared to Ubiad1+/+: :HmgcrKi/Ki littermates.
source: Compared to Ubiad1+/+: :HmgcrKi/Ki littermates, Ubiad1-/-: :HmgcrKi/Ki mice exhibited elevated levels of ALT (1.6-fold) and AST (>5 fold) in the serum (Figure 4C and D; Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is shown in the blood chemistry data in Figure 4C and D.

claim: Elevated levels of serum aminotransferases are routinely applied as biomarkers for hepatocyte injury.
source: Elevated levels of serum aminotransferases are routinely applied as biomarkers for hepatocyte injury.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: Livers of Ubiad1-deficient mice did not feature gross abnormalities upon histological analysis.
source: However, livers of Ubiad1-deficient mice did not feature gross abnormalities upon histological analysis (data not shown).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from histological analysis.

claim: Ubiad1-deficient mice exhibited a 2-fold increase in serum LDH.
source: Further examination revealed Ubiad1 deficient mice exhibited a 2-fold increase in serum LDH and a 4–7.5-fold increase in CK that was accompanied by a 35% decrease in ALP (Figure 4 and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is shown in the blood chemistry data in Figure 4D.

claim: Ubiad1-deficient mice exhibited a 4–7.5-fold increase in CK.
source: Further examination revealed Ubiad1 deficient mice exhibited a 2-fold increase in serum LDH and a 4–7.5-fold increase in CK that was accompanied by a 35% decrease in ALP (Figure 4 and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is shown in the blood chemistry data in Figure 4D.

claim: Ubiad1-deficient mice exhibited a 35% decrease in ALP.
source: Further examination revealed Ubiad1 deficient mice exhibited a 2-fold increase in serum LDH and a 4–7.5-fold increase in CK that was accompanied by a 35% decrease in ALP (Figure 4 and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is shown in the blood chemistry data in Figure 4C and D.

claim: Elevated serum LDH, CK, and decreased ALP are consistent with muscle injury and bone dysfunction in Ubiad1-/-: :HmgcrKi/Ki mice.
source: These observations are consistent with muscle injury and bone dysfunction in Ubiad1-/-: :HmgcrKi/Ki mice.
evidence: This is inferred from the blood chemistry results.

claim: Degenerating skeletal muscle myofibers with macrophage infiltration were observed by histological analysis of Ubiad1-deficient mice.
source: Indeed, degenerating skeletal muscle myofibers with macrophage infiltration and myofibers with centrally-localized nuclei as well as cell disorganization within the femoral growth plate were all observed by histological analysis of Ubiad1-deficient mice (Figure 5; Figure 5—figure supplement 1 and 2).
evidence: This is shown in the histological images in Figure 5.

claim: Myofibers with centrally-localized nuclei were observed by histological analysis of Ubiad1-deficient mice.
source: Indeed, degenerating skeletal muscle myofibers with macrophage infiltration and myofibers with centrally-localized nuclei as well as cell disorganization within the femoral growth plate were all observed by histological analysis of Ubiad1-deficient mice (Figure 5; Figure 5—figure supplement 1 and 2).
evidence: This is shown in the histological images in Figure 5.

claim: Cell disorganization within the femoral growth plate was observed by histological analysis of Ubiad1-deficient mice.
source: Indeed, degenerating skeletal muscle myofibers with macrophage infiltration and myofibers with centrally-localized nuclei as well as cell disorganization within the femoral growth plate were all observed by histological analysis of Ubiad1-deficient mice (Figure 5; Figure 5—figure supplement 1 and 2).
evidence: This is shown in the histological images in Figure 5B.

claim: Statins are competitive inhibitors of HMGCR.
source: Statins, competitive inhibitors of HMGCR, are widely prescribed to lower plasma levels of cholesterol-rich low-density lipoprotein and reduce atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: Statins are widely prescribed to lower plasma levels of cholesterol-rich low-density lipoprotein and reduce atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease.
source: Statins, competitive inhibitors of HMGCR, are widely prescribed to lower plasma levels of cholesterol-rich low-density lipoprotein and reduce atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: A significant fraction of patients undergoing statin therapy develop myopathy.
source: However, a significant fraction of patients undergoing statin therapy develop myopathy; a small portion of these patients progress to rhabdomyolysis (Thompson et al., 2003; Ward et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Thompson et al., 2003 and Ward et al., 2019.

claim: A small portion of patients with statin-induced myopathy progress to rhabdomyolysis.
source: However, a significant fraction of patients undergoing statin therapy develop myopathy; a small portion of these patients progress to rhabdomyolysis (Thompson et al., 2003; Ward et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Thompson et al., 2003 and Ward et al., 2019.

claim: Statin-induced myopathy has been attributed to depletion of mevalonate-derived metabolites resulting from inhibition of HMGCR.
source: Statin-induced myopathy has been attributed to depletion of mevalonate-derived metabolites resulting from inhibition of HMGCR.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: Skeletal muscle-specific knockout of HMGCR in mice causes severe myopathy that is rescued by mevalonate.
source: Skeletal muscle-specific knockout of HMGCR in mice causes severe myopathy that is rescued by mevalonate (Osaki et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Osaki et al., 2015.

claim: Ubiad1-/-: :HmgcrKi/Ki mice exhibit signs of muscle injury.
source: The observation that Ubiad1-/-: :HmgcrKi/Ki mice exhibit signs of muscle injury suggests statin-induced myopathy may in part, result from MK-4 depletion.
evidence: This is based on the histological and blood chemistry data presented in Figures 4 and 5.

claim: Statin-induced myopathy may in part result from MK-4 depletion.
source: The observation that Ubiad1-/-: :HmgcrKi/Ki mice exhibit signs of muscle injury suggests statin-induced myopathy may in part, result from MK-4 depletion.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the muscle injury observed in Ubiad1-deficient mice.

claim: Vitamin K modulates bone homeostasis and metabolism through two mechanisms.
source: Evidence indicates that vitamin K modulates bone homeostasis and metabolism through two mechanisms.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the discussion.

claim: One mechanism by which vitamin K modulates bone homeostasis is mediated by osteocalcin and matrix Gla protein.
source: One mechanism is mediated by osteocalcin and matrix Gla protein (Fusaro et al., 2017), two VKDPs that play key roles in bone formation and mineralization.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Fusaro et al., 2017.

claim: Osteocalcin and matrix Gla protein are two VKDPs that play key roles in bone formation and mineralization.
source: One mechanism is mediated by osteocalcin and matrix Gla protein (Fusaro et al., 2017), two VKDPs that play key roles in bone formation and mineralization.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Fusaro et al., 2017.

claim: The second mechanism by which vitamin K modulates bone homeostasis is mediated by the nuclear receptor known as steroid and xenobiotic receptor (SXR) in humans and pregnane X receptor (PXR) in mice.
source: The second mechanism is mediated by the nuclear receptor known as steroid and xenobiotic receptor (SXR) in humans and pregnane X receptor (PXR) in mice.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion.

claim: SXR and PXR are promiscuous nuclear receptors that are activated by a wide variety of xenobiotics and regulate genes involved in metabolism and clearance of the substances.
source: These promiscuous nuclear receptors are activated by a wide variety of xenobiotics and regulate genes involved in metabolism and clearance of the substances (Kliewer, 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Kliewer, 2003.

claim: Pxr-deficient mice present with osteopenia accompanied by reduced bone formation and increased bone resorption.
source: Pxr-deficient mice present with osteopenia accompanied by reduced bone formation and increased bone resorption (Azuma et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Azuma et al., 2010.

claim: MK-4 has been reported to bind to and activate PXR.
source: Considering that MK-4 has been reported to bind to and activate PXR (Tabb et al., 2003), it will be important to determine whether Ubiad1-deficiency phenocopies Pxr-deficiency with regard to bone homeostasis.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Tabb et al., 2003.

claim: Ubiad1Ki/Ki mice harbor a knockin mutation that changes asparagine-100 (N100) to serine (N100S).
source: We recently generated mice (designated Ubiad1Ki/Ki) harboring a knockin mutation that changes asparagine-100 (N100) to serine (N100S) (Jo et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Jo et al., 2019.

claim: The N100S mutation in mouse UBIAD1 corresponds to SCD-associated N102S mutation in human UBIAD1 that abolishes sensing of membrane-embedded GGpp.
source: The N100S mutation in mouse UBIAD1 corresponds to SCD-associated N102S mutation in human UBIAD1 that abolishes sensing of membrane-embedded GGpp.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion.

claim: UBIAD1 (N100S) was sequestered in ER membranes to inhibit ERAD of HMGCR, causing the protein's accumulation and overproduction of sterol and nonsterol isoprenoids in the liver and other tissues of Ubiad1Ki/Ki mice.
source: UBIAD1 (N100S) was sequestered in ER membranes to inhibit ERAD of HMGCR, causing the protein's accumulation and overproduction of sterol and nonsterol isoprenoids in the liver and other tissues of Ubiad1Ki/Ki mice.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion based on previous work.

claim: Significant corneal opacification was observed in Ubiad1Ki/Ki mice greater than 50 weeks of age.
source: Significant corneal opacification was observed in Ubiad1Ki/Ki mice greater than 50 weeks of age (HmgcrKi/Ki mice used in the current study were not aged and thus, not examined for corneal opacification).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion.

claim: These findings unequivocally position UBIAD1 as a major regulator of HMGCR and mevalonate metabolism in vivo.
source: Considered together with current studies, these findings unequivocally position UBIAD1 as a major regulator of HMGCR and mevalonate metabolism in vivo, provide new links between synthesis of sterols and MK-4, and establish Ubiad1-/-: :HmgcrKi/Ki mice as a model of MK-4 deficiency.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the collective findings of the study.

claim: These findings provide new links between synthesis of sterols and MK-4.
source: Considered together with current studies, these findings unequivocally position UBIAD1 as a major regulator of HMGCR and mevalonate metabolism in vivo, provide new links between synthesis of sterols and MK-4, and establish Ubiad1-/-: :HmgcrKi/Ki mice as a model of MK-4 deficiency.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the collective findings of the study.

claim: Ubiad1-/-: :HmgcrKi/Ki mice are established as a model of MK-4 deficiency.
source: Considered together with current studies, these findings unequivocally position UBIAD1 as a major regulator of HMGCR and mevalonate metabolism in vivo, provide new links between synthesis of sterols and MK-4, and establish Ubiad1-/-: :HmgcrKi/Ki mice as a model of MK-4 deficiency.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the collective findings of the study.

claim: HmgcrKi/Ki mice harbor homozygous nucleotide mutations in the Hmgcr gene that change lysine residues 89 and 248 to arginine.
source: Previously described HmgcrKi/Ki mice harbor homozygous nucleotide mutations in the Hmgcr gene that change lysine residues 89 and 248 to arginine (Hwang et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Hwang et al., 2016.

claim: Mutations in HmgcrKi/Ki mice prevent Insig-mediated ubiquitination and subsequent ERAD of HMGCR in the liver and other tissues of the knockin mice.
source: These mutations prevent Insig-mediated ubiquitination and subsequent ERAD of HMGCR in the liver and other tissues of the knockin mice.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: Ubiad1 deficiency led to the disorganization of cells within proliferative and hypertrophic zones of the growth plate.
source: The results reveal that Ubiad1 deficiency led to the disorganization of cells within proliferative and hypertrophic zones of the growth plate, persistence of cartilage within trabeculae, and a mild decrease in the number of boney trabeculae.
evidence: This is shown in the histological images in Figure 5B.

claim: Ubiad1 deficiency led to persistence of cartilage within trabeculae.
source: The results reveal that Ubiad1 deficiency led to the disorganization of cells within proliferative and hypertrophic zones of the growth plate, persistence of cartilage within trabeculae, and a mild decrease in the number of boney trabeculae.
evidence: This is shown in the histological images in Figure 5B.

claim: Ubiad1 deficiency led to a mild decrease in the number of boney trabeculae.
source: The results reveal that Ubiad1 deficiency led to the disorganization of cells within proliferative and hypertrophic zones of the growth plate, persistence of cartilage within trabeculae, and a mild decrease in the number of boney trabeculae.
evidence: This is shown in the histological images in Figure 5B.

claim: Genetic ablation of UBIAD1 in transformed human fibroblasts led to enhanced ERAD of HMGCR and reduced cholesterol synthesis and intracellular accumulation of cholesterol.
source: The genetic ablation of UBIAD1 in transformed human fibroblasts led to enhanced ERAD of HMGCR and reduced cholesterol synthesis and intracellular accumulation of cholesterol (Schumacher et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Schumacher et al., 2018.

claim: Homozygous Hmgcr deficiency caused early embryonic lethality in mice.
source: Indeed, homozygous Hmgcr deficiency caused early embryonic lethality in mice (Ohashi et al., 2003), establishing that mevalonate-derived metabolites are crucial for embryonic development.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Ohashi et al., 2003.

claim: Mevalonate-derived metabolites are crucial for embryonic development.
source: Indeed, homozygous Hmgcr deficiency caused early embryonic lethality in mice (Ohashi et al., 2003), establishing that mevalonate-derived metabolites are crucial for embryonic development.
evidence: This is inferred from the embryonic lethality caused by Hmgcr deficiency.

claim: HMGCR protein accumulated in tissues of HmgcrKi/Ki mice that stimulated the overproduction of cholesterol and likely other sterol and nonsterol isoprenoids.
source: As a result of resistance to ERAD, HMGCR protein accumulated in tissues of HmgcrKi/Ki mice that stimulated the overproduction of cholesterol and likely other sterol and nonsterol isoprenoids.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion based on previous work.

claim: Overproduction of sterol and nonsterol isoprenoids in HmgcrKi/Ki mice would rescue embryonic lethality associated with Ubiad1 deficiency.
source: Hence, we reasoned that overproduction of sterol and nonsterol isoprenoids in HmgcrKi/Ki mice would rescue embryonic lethality associated with Ubiad1 deficiency.
evidence: This is the hypothesis tested in the study.

claim: Administration of MK-4, ubiquinone-10, or cholesterol to Ubiad1+/- mice prior to intercrossing and throughout pregnancy failed to rescue embryonic lethality of Ubiad1 deficiency.
source: Notably, administration of MK-4, ubiquinone-10 (Nakagawa et al., 2014), or cholesterol (data not shown) to Ubiad1+/- mice prior to intercrossing and throughout pregnancy failed to rescue embryonic lethality of Ubiad1 deficiency.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study.

claim: Genes encoding HMGCR, enzymes required for GGpp and Fpp synthesis, and prenylation of small GTPases are essential for migration of primordial germ cells during embryonic development.
source: While the identity of the mevalonate-derived metabolite(s) that rescues embryonic development remains unknown, genes encoding HMGCR, enzymes required for GGpp and Fpp synthesis, and prenylation of small GTPases are essential for migration of primordial germ cells during embryonic development (Kunwar et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Kunwar et al., 2006.

claim: Depletion of GGpp and/or Fpp owing to enhanced ERAD of HMGCR and reduced prenylation of small GTPases may contribute to embryonic lethality associated with Ubiad1 deficiency.
source: Thus, depletion of GGpp and/or Fpp owing to enhanced ERAD of HMGCR and reduced prenylation of small GTPases may contribute to embryonic lethality associated with Ubiad1 deficiency.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the known roles of GGpp and Fpp.

claim: Despite the absence of MK-4, Ubiad1-deficient mice did not exhibit typical signs of vitamin K deficiency (i.e., excessive hemorrhaging).
source: However, it is important to note that despite the absence of MK-4, Ubiad1-deficient mice did not exhibit typical signs of vitamin K deficiency (i.e., excessive hemorrhaging).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study.

claim: The diet used in this study is supplemented with MD, which does not exhibit vitamin K activity and is not converted to MK-4 in absence of UBIAD1.
source: The diet used in this study is supplemented with MD, which does not exhibit vitamin K activity (Buitenhuis et al., 1990) and is not converted to MK-4 in absence of UBIAD1.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citation to Buitenhuis et al., 1990.

claim: The diet and/or gut microbiota provide sufficient amounts of vitamin K to support γ-glutamyl carboxylation of coagulation factors in Ubiad1-/-: :HmgcrKi/Ki mice.
source: This indicates that the diet and/or gut microbiota provide sufficient amounts of vitamin K to support γ-glutamyl carboxylation of coagulation factors in Ubiad1-/-: :HmgcrKi/Ki mice, suggesting their failure to thrive may result from disruption of carboxylation-independent activities of MK-4.
evidence: This is inferred from the absence of hemorrhaging in Ubiad1-deficient mice.

claim: Failure of Ubiad1-deficient mice to thrive may result from disruption of carboxylation-independent activities of MK-4.
source: This indicates that the diet and/or gut microbiota provide sufficient amounts of vitamin K to support γ-glutamyl carboxylation of coagulation factors in Ubiad1-/-: :HmgcrKi/Ki mice, suggesting their failure to thrive may result from disruption of carboxylation-independent activities of MK-4.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the phenotype of Ubiad1-deficient mice.

claim: Levels of MK-4 were highest in the pancreas and brain.
source: Figure 4B shows that similar to previous results (Harshman et al., 2016; Okano et al., 2008), levels of MK-4 were highest in the pancreas and brain.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4B and supported by citations to Harshman et al., 2016 and Okano et al., 2008.

claim: Failure of Ubiad1-deficient mice to thrive may result from reduced production of MK-4 in the pancreas, brain, or other tissues.
source: Thus, failure of Ubiad1-deficient mice to thrive may result from reduced production of MK-4 in these or other tissues of the animals.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the high levels of MK-4 in pancreas and brain.

claim: Inducible knockout of Ubiad1 in adult mice caused death within 60 days.
source: Recent studies show that inducible knockout of Ubiad1 in adult mice caused death within 60 days (Nakagawa et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Nakagawa et al., 2019.

claim: The most striking abnormality of inducible Ubiad1 knockout mice was a remarkable reduction in pancreas size resulting from apoptotic disappearance of acinar cells.
source: The most striking abnormality of these mice was a remarkable reduction in pancreas size resulting from apoptotic disappearance of acinar cells.
evidence: This is stated based on findings from Nakagawa et al., 2019.

claim: UBIAD1-mediated synthesis of MK-4 is essential for survival of pancreatic acinar cells.
source: This observation prompted the authors to conclude that UBIAD1-mediated synthesis of MK-4 is essential for survival of pancreatic acinar cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion from Nakagawa et al., 2019.

claim: The pancreas of Ubiad1-/-: :HmgcrKi/Ki mice failed to produce MK-4.
source: Our current studies reveal that the pancreas of Ubiad1-/-: :HmgcrKi/Ki mice failed to produce MK-4 (Figure 4B); however, the organ was normal in size and exhibited no gross abnormalities (data not shown).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The pancreas of Ubiad1-/-: :HmgcrKi/Ki mice was normal in size and exhibited no gross abnormalities.
source: Our current studies reveal that the pancreas of Ubiad1-/-: :HmgcrKi/Ki mice failed to produce MK-4 (Figure 4B); however, the organ was normal in size and exhibited no gross abnormalities (data not shown).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study.

claim: Ubiquitination/ERAD-resistant HMGCR allows for production of sterol and/or nonsterol isoprenoids distinct from MK-4 that are essential for subsistence of pancreatic acinar cells.
source: These findings argue that ubiquitination/ERAD-resistant HMGCR allows for production of sterol and/or nonsterol isoprenoids distinct from MK-4 that are essential for subsistence of pancreatic acinar cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the normal pancreas in Ubiad1-/-: :HmgcrKi/Ki mice despite absence of MK-4.

claim: Serum cholesterol levels were not significantly different between Ubiad1+/+: :HmgcrKi/Ki and Ubiad1-/-: :HmgcrKi/Ki male mice.
source: Serum cholesterol levels were not significantly different between the two groups of male mice (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4C.

source: Modest, but significant increases in levels of triglycerides (55%) and nonesterified fatty acids (46%) were observed in the serum of Ubiad1-/-: :HmgcrKi/Ki mice compared to Ubiad1+/+: :HmgcrKi/Ki littermates.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Modest, but significant increases in levels of nonesterified fatty acids (46%) were observed in the serum of Ubiad1-/-: :HmgcrKi/Ki mice compared to Ubiad1+/+: :HmgcrKi/Ki littermates.
source: Modest, but significant increases in levels of triglycerides (55%) and nonesterified fatty acids (46%) were observed in the serum of Ubiad1-/-: :HmgcrKi/Ki mice compared to Ubiad1+/+: :HmgcrKi/Ki littermates.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Ubiad1-deficient mice exhibited larger increases in serum levels of alanine aminotransferase (ALT) (174%).
source: The Ubiad1-deficient mice exhibited larger increases in serum levels of two classic markers of liver injury, alanine aminotransferase (ALT) (174%) and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) (583%); serum alkaline phosphatase (ALP) was reduced approximately 35%.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Ubiad1-deficient mice exhibited larger increases in serum levels of aspartate aminotransferase (AST) (583%).
source: The Ubiad1-deficient mice exhibited larger increases in serum levels of two classic markers of liver injury, alanine aminotransferase (ALT) (174%) and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) (583%); serum alkaline phosphatase (ALP) was reduced approximately 35%.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Serum alkaline phosphatase (ALP) was reduced approximately 35% in Ubiad1-deficient mice.
source: The Ubiad1-deficient mice exhibited larger increases in serum levels of two classic markers of liver injury, alanine aminotransferase (ALT) (174%) and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) (583%); serum alkaline phosphatase (ALP) was reduced approximately 35%.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Serum levels of AST were elevated 5-fold in Ubiad1-deficient mice.
source: Similar to results of Figure 4C, serum levels of AST and ALT were elevated 5-fold and 1.8-fold, respectively, in the absence of Ubiad1 (Figure 4D).

claim: Serum levels of ALT were elevated 1.8-fold in Ubiad1-deficient mice.
source: Similar to results of Figure 4C, serum levels of AST and ALT were elevated 5-fold and 1.8-fold, respectively, in the absence of Ubiad1 (Figure 4D).

claim: Serum lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) was elevated approximately 2-fold in Ubiad1-deficient mice.
source: Serum lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) was elevated approximately 2-fold in Ubiad1-deficient mice; however, a more prominent elevation (7.5-fold) of serum creatine kinase (CK) was observed.

claim: A more prominent elevation (7.5-fold) of serum creatine kinase (CK) was observed in Ubiad1-deficient mice.
source: Serum lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) was elevated approximately 2-fold in Ubiad1-deficient mice; however, a more prominent elevation (7.5-fold) of serum creatine kinase (CK) was observed.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4D.

claim: A slight reduction in the amount of serum lipase was present in Ubiad1-deficient mice.
source: Finally, a slight reduction in the amount of serum lipase and amylase was present in Ubiad1-deficient mice; serum albumin remained unchanged.

claim: A slight reduction in the amount of serum amylase was present in Ubiad1-deficient mice.

claim: Serum albumin remained unchanged in Ubiad1-deficient mice.

claim: Abnormalities were observed in only two tissues of Ubiad1-deficient mice – skeletal muscle and bone.
source: Surprisingly, abnormalities were observed in only two tissues of Ubiad1-deficient mice – skeletal muscle and bone.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the histological analysis.

claim: H and E-staining of gastrocnemius and quadriceps muscles from male Ubiad1-deficient mice revealed occasional degenerating myofibers with macrophage infiltration.
source: Hematoxylin and eosin (H and E)-staining of gastrocnemius (Figure 5A, panels 1–4) and quadriceps muscles (panels 5–8) from male Ubiad1-deficient mice revealed occasional degenerating myofibers with macrophage infiltration as well as frequent myofibers with centrally-localized nuclei.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5A.

claim: H and E-staining of gastrocnemius and quadriceps muscles from male Ubiad1-deficient mice revealed frequent myofibers with centrally-localized nuclei.
source: Hematoxylin and eosin (H and E)-staining of gastrocnemius (Figure 5A, panels 1–4) and quadriceps muscles (panels 5–8) from male Ubiad1-deficient mice revealed occasional degenerating myofibers with macrophage infiltration as well as frequent myofibers with centrally-localized nuclei.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Histological findings in muscle are indicative of ongoing muscle injury and correlate to the elevated serum CK levels.
source: Overall, these histological findings are indicative of ongoing muscle injury and correlate to the elevated serum CK levels observed in Figure 4D.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the histological findings in relation to blood chemistry data.

claim: SREBPs are transcription factors synthesized as inactive, ER-bound precursors.
source: Sterol regulatory element-binding protein (SREBP)−1 and −2 are transcription factors synthesized as inactive, ER-bound precursors (Brown and Goldstein, 1997).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Brown and Goldstein, 1997.

claim: Upon lipid deprivation, transcriptionally active fragments of SREBPs are proteolytically released from membranes and migrate to the nucleus where they activate transcription of genes encoding cholesterol and fatty acid synthetic enzymes.
source: Upon lipid deprivation, transcriptionally active fragments of SREBPs are proteolytically released from membranes and migrate to the nucleus where they activate transcription of genes encoding cholesterol and fatty acid synthetic enzymes (Horton et al., 2003).
